declarations.name: FfiCapsuleClient
declarations.doc:
The unauthenticated entry point over the SDK's auth + upload endpoints. Turns
credentials into an [`FfiSession`] handle; the protocol pin and endpoints are
captured once here and reused by every session this client mints.

members.name: init
members.signature: public convenience init(authBaseUrl: String, uploadBaseUrl: String, protocolVersion: String, cohortHash: String?) throws
members.doc:
Build a client.

- `auth_base_url` is the auth endpoint root (e.g. `https://api.example.com/auth`).
- `upload_base_url` is the upload endpoint root (`POST` target; chunk/HEAD hang
under `{upload_base_url}/{id}`).
- `protocol_version` is the pinned protocol date (`YYYY-MM-DD`).
- `cohort_hash` is the optional advisory device-cohort digest; `None`
sends nothing (the server behaves identically).

members.name: login
members.signature: func login(email: String, password: String) async throws -> FfiLoginOutcome
members.doc: Authenticate with email + password, returning an authenticated session handle.

members.name: register
members.signature: func register(email: String, password: String) async throws -> FfiSession
members.doc:
Create an account and return an authenticated session handle (the server
issues tokens on registration).
An address and a password, and nothing else: the server takes nothing else.
A display name is a fact about a person, and the profile surface that would hold one is
owed rather than assumed.

members.name: verifySecondFactor
members.signature: func verifySecondFactor(mfaToken: String, totpCode: String) async throws -> FfiSession
members.doc:
Complete a sign-in with the code an authenticator app is showing.

`mfa_token` is what [`FfiLoginOutcome::SecondFactorRequired`] carried. It is good once
and for five minutes.

declarations.name: FfiHardwareKeyAgreement
declarations.doc:
The per-platform **key-agreement** element (Secure Enclave `P256.KeyAgreement`, StrongBox
ECDH, TPM 2.0 ECDH), implemented by native Swift/Kotlin over the uniffi foreign-trait
boundary — the ECDH analogue of [`FfiHardwareSigner`], and this namespace's declaration of
`capsule-core`'s `HardwareKeyAgreement` contract.

It backs the hardware-bound classical half of the device **encryption** key:
the element holds a static P-256 private key and performs the ECDH, so the scalar never
leaves hardware, while Rust drives the software-sealed ML-KEM-768 half and the hybrid
combiner. Failures reuse [`FfiHardwareSignerError`], exactly as core's trait reuses its
signer error.

members.name: enroll
members.doc:
Generate (or bind to) the hardware P-256 key-agreement keypair for `key_alias`,
returning its public key as **uncompressed SEC1** (`0x04‖x‖y`, 65 bytes). Idempotent per
alias.

members.name: publicKey
members.doc: The uncompressed-SEC1 P-256 public key for an already-enrolled `key_alias`.

members.name: keyAgreement
members.signature: func keyAgreement(keyAlias: String, peerPublic: Data) throws -> Data
members.doc:
ECDH against `peer_public` (the sender's ephemeral P-256 public key, uncompressed SEC1)
with the hardware key for `key_alias`, returning the **raw 32-byte shared secret** (the
big-endian x-coordinate, before any KDF).

members.name: assertNonExportable
members.doc:
Non-exportability assertion: a conforming element MUST refuse to reveal the private
bytes, returning [`FfiHardwareSignerError::Exportable`] if they can be read.

declarations.name: FfiHardwareSigner
declarations.doc:
The per-platform secure element (Secure Enclave, StrongBox, TPM), implemented by native
Swift/Kotlin over the uniffi foreign-trait boundary.

The byte shapes are fixed by the constructor the element is handed to, not by the trait:

- [`FfiWorkspace::create_with_p256_hardware_signer`] — the **P-256** shape shipping
elements actually provide: [`enroll`](Self::enroll) /
[`classical_public_key`](Self::classical_public_key) return a SEC1 public key and
[`sign_classical`](Self::sign_classical) a **DER-encoded ECDSA** signature over
`SHA-256(msg)`.
- [`FfiWorkspace::create_with_hardware_signer`] — the **Ed25519** shape: a 32-byte public
key and a 64-byte signature over `msg`. No shipping secure element holds Ed25519 keys, so
this is the software/TPM reference path.

Either way Rust composes the classical half with a software-sealed ML-DSA-65 half into the
published hybrid device key.

members.name: enroll
members.doc:
Generate (or bind to) the hardware keypair for `key_alias`, returning its public key in
the constructor's shape: a SEC1 P-256 key for
[`FfiWorkspace::create_with_p256_hardware_signer`], a 32-byte Ed25519 key for
[`FfiWorkspace::create_with_hardware_signer`]. Idempotent per alias.

members.name: classicalPublicKey
members.doc:
The public key for an already-enrolled `key_alias`, in the same constructor-dependent
shape [`enroll`](Self::enroll) returns (SEC1 P-256, or 32-byte Ed25519).

members.name: signClassical
members.signature: func signClassical(keyAlias: String, msg: Data) throws -> Data
members.doc:
Sign `msg` with the hardware key for `key_alias`, in the constructor's shape: a
DER-encoded ECDSA signature over `SHA-256(msg)` for
[`FfiWorkspace::create_with_p256_hardware_signer`], a 64-byte Ed25519 signature over
`msg` for [`FfiWorkspace::create_with_hardware_signer`].

members.name: assertNonExportable
members.doc:
Non-exportability assertion: a conforming element MUST refuse to reveal the private
bytes, returning [`FfiHardwareSignerError::Exportable`] if they can be read.

declarations.name: FfiSession
declarations.doc:
An authenticated session handle. Owns the SDK token store internally (auto
pre-flight refresh, single-flight, `401`-retry-once); **no token ever crosses
the FFI boundary**. Every flow rides this handle.

members.name: escrowGet
members.signature: func escrowGet(apiBaseUrl: String) async throws -> Data
members.doc:
Fetch this account's escrow blob (`GET /v1/auth/escrow`) as opaque canonical CBOR — the
bytes [`FfiWorkspace::verify_escrow_blob`](FfiWorkspace::verify_escrow_blob) checks and
a recovery flow unwraps.

No escrow enrolled yet is [`FfiError::Escrow`] carrying `error.escrow.not_stored` — the
code that separates "set up a recovery key" from "we could not read the one you have".
A refused credential is [`FfiError::Auth`].

members.name: escrowPut
members.signature: func escrowPut(apiBaseUrl: String, blob: Data) async throws -> FfiEscrowStored
members.doc:
Store or replace this account's **master-key escrow blob** (`PUT /v1/auth/escrow`).
`blob` is the opaque canonical CBOR
[`FfiWorkspace::escrow_blob`](FfiWorkspace::escrow_blob) minted — the master key itself
never crosses this boundary in either direction.

Single active escrow: the server replaces any prior blob in the same transaction, so the
secret a rotation retired unwraps nothing.

`api_base_url` is the API root the session authenticates against (the per-call endpoint
convention this surface already uses for `sync_pull`). A URL operation paths cannot hang
off is [`FfiError::InvalidArgument`]; a refused credential is [`FfiError::Auth`], so a
caller re-authenticates rather than retrying; everything else is
[`FfiError::Escrow`] with the server's `error.escrow.*` code when it sent one.

The answer says what the store did: [`FfiEscrowStored::replaced`] separates "recovery
set up" from "recovery key replaced" (the previous secret has stopped working).

members.name: fetchBlobToPath
members.signature: func fetchBlobToPath(blobBaseUrl: String, hash: String, size: UInt64, path: String) async throws
members.doc:
**Fetch** the blob at content address `hash` (`size` bytes, as the sync feed's
[`FfiBlobRef`] declares) into the file at `path`, created or truncated.

The blob streams to disk in bounded `Range` windows, so memory is bounded by one window
whatever the blob's size, and its content address is checked as it lands. On any error
the file is removed: a path this returns `Ok` for holds exactly the verified ciphertext.
A session that cannot authorize the fetch is [`FfiError::Auth`], so the app signs in
again; every other failure is [`FfiError::Fetch`].

`blob_base_url` is the root the blob route hangs off (`{blob_base_url}/blob/{hash}`),
the server's `/v1` root.

members.name: fetchDeviceDirectory
members.signature: func fetchDeviceDirectory(apiBaseUrl: String, userId: String, pinnedUserIk: Data) async throws -> Data
members.doc:
Fetch a user's signed device directory, **verified under `pinned_user_ik`** (the bytes
[`FfiWorkspace::user_ik_public`](FfiWorkspace::user_ik_public) returns) before it is
handed back. A document that does not verify is an error, never a return value.

members.name: isAuthenticated
members.doc: Whether the session currently holds tokens (`false` after logout).

members.name: logout
members.doc: Revoke the session server-side and clear the local store (idempotent).

members.name: publishDeviceDirectory
members.signature: func publishDeviceDirectory(apiBaseUrl: String, directoryCbor: Data, userIk: Data) async throws -> UInt64
members.doc:
Publish this device's **signed device directory**, returning the `directory_version` the
server now stores. `directory_cbor` is the opaque document
[`FfiWorkspace::signed_device_directory`](FfiWorkspace::signed_device_directory)
produced; it travels verbatim, because re-encoding it would detach it from the signature
it carries. `user_ik` is the account's user identity **public** key the document is
signed under — the bytes [`FfiWorkspace::user_ik_public`](FfiWorkspace::user_ik_public)
returns — which the server anchors on first publish and verifies every publish against.

Publish when the document changes (a device enrolled or revoked). The version must
advance — republishing an unchanged document answers the version-conflict code.

members.name: pushAsset
members.signature: func pushAsset(workspace: FfiWorkspace, assetId: String) async throws -> FfiPushReport
members.doc:
**Push** one sealed asset of `workspace` — every blob of its bundle, in ladder order
(provenance and metadata, then derivative manifests and derivatives, then the
original) — driving `capsule_sdk::push::push_bundle` inside the SDK.

The original never crosses the boundary: its ciphertext is re-derived from the
plaintext on disk one upload chunk window at a time, so memory is bounded by the
transfer window whatever the original's size. The workspace lock is held only while the
bundle is built, never across the network.

Every blob is driven; one the server already holds answers `duplicate_blob` and comes
back [`FfiUploadOutcome::AlreadyStored`], so pushing twice is safe. The album must
already be provisioned on the server.

**A create the server refused is re-sealed and retried once** (issue #822). When the
album's epoch moved past the one the asset was sealed under, the server refuses its
create for good; if this device holds a newer epoch, the asset is re-sealed at it
(`Workspace::reseal_create`) and pushed again, once. A second refusal fails the push.
When this device holds no newer epoch the push fails with [`FfiError::Upload`] carrying
the server's code and a detail saying there is no newer epoch to re-seal at, and the
asset stays local. That detail names no missing key: the refusal may have had nothing to
do with the epoch (a revoked device, withdrawn write access), or another device rotated
the album and its key has not reached this one yet.

members.name: syncPull
members.signature: func syncPull(apiBaseUrl: String, cursor: Data, pageSize: UInt32) async throws -> FfiSyncPage
members.doc:
Pull one page of the key-free sync feed after `cursor` from `api_base_url`
(`http[s]://host:port`). Pass an empty `cursor` for the first page; persist and pass
back `next_cursor` to advance. The bearer rides the `Authorization` header
(auto-refreshed); it never crosses the FFI boundary.

The parameter is the **API base URL** now, not a gRPC endpoint: the feed is
`GET /v1/sync` on the same origin as every other call.

members.name: upload
members.signature: func upload(request: FfiUploadRequest, data: Data) async throws -> FfiUploadOutcome
members.doc:
Upload a full ciphertext blob (`data`) under `request`, driving the adaptive,
resumable protocol with the code-driven recovery matrix.

`data` crosses the boundary whole, so this is for blobs an app already holds in memory.
To push a sealed asset, original included, use [`push_asset`](Self::push_asset), which
never holds the original whole.

members.name: uploadStatus
members.signature: func uploadStatus(sessionId: String) async throws -> FfiUploadStatus?
members.doc:
Query an upload session's progress (`HEAD /upload/{id}`). `None` means the
session is gone (discarded/expired/never-existent).

declarations.name: FfiWorkspace
declarations.doc:
A Capsule workspace, callable from Swift/Kotlin: the durable library at a filesystem root
plus everything an app does with it.

`Workspace` mutates through `&mut self` while uniffi objects expose only `&self`; the
`Mutex` supplies the interior mutability and serializes concurrent foreign calls.

members.name: create
members.signature: public static func create(root: String, passphrase: Data, tier: FfiDeviceTier, client: FfiClientBuild) throws -> FfiWorkspace
members.doc:
**Enroll**: create a brand-new library at `root`, guarded by `passphrase` at the
Argon2id cost for `tier`. Mints the account, the device key, and the signed device
directory, and seeds the durable album keystore.

`client` is the app's own build identity: every manifest this workspace authors then
reports `client_id/semver+commit` rather than the bare `capsule-core` default.

members.name: createWithHardwareSigner
members.signature: public static func createWithHardwareSigner(root: String, passphrase: Data, tier: FfiDeviceTier, hardware: FfiHardwareSigner, keyAlias: String, mlSeed: Data, client: FfiClientBuild) throws -> FfiWorkspace
members.doc:
**Enroll with a hardware-bound Ed25519 device key**: as [`create`](Self::create), but
the classical half of the device signing key is produced by `hardware` under
`key_alias` over **Ed25519** (a 32-byte public key, 64-byte signatures). The
post-quantum ML-DSA-65 half is the software-sealed `ml_seed` (32 bytes).

No shipping secure element holds Ed25519 keys, so this is the software/TPM reference
composition; phones use
[`create_with_p256_hardware_signer`](Self::create_with_p256_hardware_signer). It is the
same core call (`HardwareBackedSigner::enroll`) reached through this namespace's
[`FfiHardwareSigner`] seam.

members.name: createWithP256HardwareSigner
members.signature: public static func createWithP256HardwareSigner(root: String, passphrase: Data, tier: FfiDeviceTier, hardware: FfiHardwareSigner, keyAlias: String, mlSeed: Data, client: FfiClientBuild) throws -> FfiWorkspace
members.doc:
**Enroll with a hardware-bound device key**: as [`create`](Self::create), but the
classical half of the device signing key is produced by `hardware` (a native Secure
Enclave / StrongBox / TPM element) under `key_alias`, over **ECDSA-P256** — the
composition shipping secure elements actually provide, none of which do Ed25519. The
post-quantum ML-DSA-65 half is the software-sealed `ml_seed` (32 bytes).

The published device key carries the P-256 tag and `verify_asset` dispatches on it, so
this is constructor parity with `capsule-core`'s own
`create_with_p256_hardware_signer` — the same core call, reached through this
namespace's [`FfiHardwareSigner`] seam.

members.name: open
members.signature: public static func `open`(root: String, passphrase: Data, tier: FfiDeviceTier, client: FfiClientBuild) throws -> FfiWorkspace
members.doc:
**Open** the existing library at `root` under `passphrase`, restoring its album keys and
authorities, every managed asset, and the `add_id` counter from disk. This is
what makes an app relaunch resume rather than re-enroll.

members.name: albums
members.doc: Every album this workspace holds key material for.

members.name: applySyncEntry
members.doc:
**Sync-apply**: verify one remote feed entry through the `verify_asset` chokepoint,
bind and decrypt its metadata blob, and return either the facts to upsert or a named
quarantine/hold verdict.

Never silently drops and never silently accepts: a refused entry is a
[`FfiSyncApplyOutcome::Quarantined`] the app must surface, not an error that aborts the
page. Errors are reserved for a failure of this workspace itself.

members.name: applySyncEntryFromFile
members.signature: func applySyncEntryFromFile(entry: FfiSyncHead, ciphertextPath: String) throws -> FfiSyncApplyOutcome
members.doc:
[`apply_sync_entry`](Self::apply_sync_entry) for an entry whose original ciphertext is
the file at `ciphertext_path` — the one
[`FfiSession::fetch_blob_to_path`](crate::ffi::FfiSession::fetch_blob_to_path) wrote —
read in memory bounded by one STREAM chunk whatever the original's size.

The same chokepoint and verdicts: the file is hashed, and that digest is what the
content-integrity step checks against the manifest's content address, so a file that is
not the committed ciphertext is quarantined as `Rejected.CiphertextHashMismatch`, as
`apply_sync_entry` quarantines those bytes. Nothing is written anywhere.

A malformed `album_id` or `local_chain_head` is refused before the file is opened, so a
bad argument never costs a read of the original. The file is hashed before the workspace
is locked, so other verbs are not held up while a large original is read.

members.name: assetIds
members.doc: Every managed asset id (UUID strings).

members.name: createAlbum
members.doc:
Create an album (minting AMK_v1, its write-tier and admin keys, and an attested
authority, then persisting the keystore). Returns the album id.

members.name: defaultAlbumId
members.doc:
The default album's id, derived deterministically from the account master key — so every
device of this account computes the same value with nothing to synchronize.

members.name: deviceId
members.doc:
This device's id (UUID string) — the `created_by_device` of every manifest it authors,
and the id to report as the session's `device_id`.

members.name: ensureAlbum
members.signature: func ensureAlbum(albumId: String, name: String) throws -> String
members.doc:
Resolve `album_id` to the album this workspace already holds, or create it under `name`.
This is the verb first-run wiring wants for the default album: it is idempotent across
relaunches, where [`create_album`](Self::create_album) would refuse.

members.name: escrowBlob
members.signature: func escrowBlob(recoverySecret: Data, tier: FfiDeviceTier) throws -> Data
members.doc:
Mint the **master-key escrow blob** under `recovery_secret`, as opaque canonical CBOR —
the bytes [`FfiSession::escrow_put`](crate::ffi::FfiSession::escrow_put) stores.

The master key never crosses this boundary: it is wrapped inside `capsule-core` and only
the wrapped blob comes out. `recovery_secret` is the ≥128-bit secret shown to the user
exactly once at first-device enrollment.

members.name: openSyncedOriginal
members.signature: func openSyncedOriginal(entry: FfiSyncHead, ciphertextPath: String, destinationPath: String) throws -> FfiOpenedOriginal
members.doc:
**Open a synced original** from the ciphertext file at `ciphertext_path` to its plaintext
at `destination_path`, in memory bounded by a few STREAM chunks whatever its size.

The entry goes through the chokepoint as
[`apply_sync_entry_from_file`](Self::apply_sync_entry_from_file) would take it, then the
file is hashed while it is decrypted: it opens only if it is the ciphertext the manifest
commits to, every chunk authenticates, and the plaintext hashes to the signed sidecar's
digest. The plaintext is written to a hidden staging file beside the destination and
renamed into place only once all of that holds, so `destination_path` is untouched by
any other verdict and never holds a partial or unverified original. An existing file there
is replaced only by a verified one.

The workspace stays locked while the original decrypts.

# Errors

[`FfiError::Workspace`] when a file cannot be read or written, or the workspace itself
fails; [`FfiError::InvalidArgument`] for a malformed entry or a destination with no file
name. A refused entry is a verdict, never an error.

members.name: provenanceHead
members.doc:
The asset's **head provenance record** as opaque canonical CBOR — the exact bytes the
`provenance` blob carries, the feed serves back as `manifest_cbor`, and a receiving
device runs through [`apply_sync_entry`](Self::apply_sync_entry).

The record wraps the head signed manifest with its chain position. That wrapper is not
optional: the server's chain head is the SHA-256 of these bytes while a client's next
`prior_provenance_hash` is the record's own hash, so the bare manifest is the one
encoding under which no lifecycle op can ever chain. Canonical CBOR is deterministic, so
the manifest inside is byte-identical to its own signed bytes — nothing is re-authored
and the two signatures still verify over exactly what they covered.

Use [`signed_manifest`](Self::signed_manifest) when the *manifest* is what is wanted.

members.name: readPlaintext
members.doc:
The plaintext bytes of a managed asset (what a gallery renders for a locally-held
original).

members.name: sealAsset
members.signature: func sealAsset(albumId: String, fileName: String, bytes: Data) throws -> String
members.doc:
**Seal + import**: take bytes the app already holds (a PhotoKit / MediaStore export),
derive the file key, STREAM-encrypt, author and sign the create manifest, seal the
signed sidecar into its metadata blob, append the provenance chain, and self-verify
through the `verify_asset` chokepoint. Returns the asset id.

`file_name` is consulted for its extension and nothing else. One call, one core call:
the whole sealing order is `capsule-core`'s.

members.name: signedDeviceDirectory
members.doc:
This workspace's **signed device directory** as opaque canonical CBOR — the bytes
[`FfiSession::publish_device_directory`](crate::ffi::FfiSession::publish_device_directory)
sends. Until this is published, every asset this device signs is an unknown device to
every other device, so first-device enrollment publishes before it uploads.

members.name: signedManifest
members.doc:
The asset's **head signed manifest** as opaque canonical CBOR.

This is a serialization of an already-signed structure, not a re-authoring: the two
signatures the manifest carries are covered by these bytes, which is why they travel
verbatim and are never re-modeled on any wire.

**Not what the sync feed carries** — that is
[`provenance_head`](Self::provenance_head), the record that wraps this manifest with its
chain position. Handing these bytes to
[`apply_sync_entry`](Self::apply_sync_entry) is refused as malformed.

members.name: uploadBlobs
members.doc:
Everything needed to push one sealed asset, in ladder order: for each blob, the
`POST /upload` body (manifest envelope projected per the server's invariant-15 rule)
and the bytes. Feed each straight to
[`FfiSession::upload`](crate::ffi::FfiSession::upload).

The index tier (`T0`) is **two** blobs — the provenance record then the sealed metadata
blob — because the server publishes an asset to other devices only once it holds both
roles. Push all of them: an app that stopped after the metadata blob would upload an
asset no device, its own included, could ever see.

The original's ciphertext is re-derived from the manifest's recorded nonce prefix and
gated on the manifest's own content address, so what reaches the network is what the
signed manifest vouches for.

Every blob comes back whole, the original included. To push without holding the
original in memory, use [`FfiSession::push_asset`](crate::ffi::FfiSession::push_asset).

members.name: userId
members.doc: The account owner's user id (UUID string).

members.name: userIkPublic
members.doc:
This account's user identity **public** key — the pin a fetched device directory is
verified against.

members.name: verifyAsset
members.doc:
Run the `verify_asset` chokepoint over a managed asset, regenerating its ciphertext
deterministically. This is the same single chokepoint sync-apply routes through — it is
exposed here so an app can re-check its own library (an integrity sweep), never as a
second verification path.

members.name: verifyEscrowBlob
members.signature: func verifyEscrowBlob(blob: Data, recoverySecret: Data) throws -> Bool
members.doc:
Local, network-free check that `recovery_secret` still opens `blob` to *this* device's
master key — the recovery verification cadence's predicate. `blob` is the canonical CBOR
[`FfiSession::escrow_get`](crate::ffi::FfiSession::escrow_get) returns.

A `false` is not necessarily a wrong secret: the cached blob may be stale after a
rotation on another device, so refresh it and re-check once before telling the user
anything.

declarations.name: FfiAlbum
declarations.doc: One album this workspace holds key material for.

members.name: albumId
members.doc: Album id (UUID string).

members.name: name
members.doc: Display name, which lives only in the client's own state — it never crosses the wire.

declarations.name: FfiAlert
declarations.doc:
One alert that is true at an instant.

Never a localized string: `class` selects the app's own `notification.*` catalog key and
`params` are interpolated into it, so a server can neither supply nor influence the words a
user reads.

members.name: class
members.doc: Which alert this is.

members.name: severity
members.doc: How prominently to present it.

members.name: deadline
members.doc:
The instant whose passing made this alert true (RFC 3339), for the two pre-armable
classes; `None` for the three whose condition is server-held.

members.name: params
members.doc:
Catalog parameters — `count`, `days_behind`, `grace`, and the pair
`recovery_check_due` always carries: `snooze_budget` (`available` / `spent`) and
`recovery` (`check` / `rewrap`).

declarations.name: FfiAssetFacts
declarations.doc: The verified facts one applied entry contributes, flattened for a catalog upsert.

members.name: assetId
members.doc: The asset id (UUID string).

members.name: albumId
members.doc: The album id (UUID string).

members.name: amkVersion
members.doc: The AMK epoch the asset is sealed under.

members.name: ciphertextHash
members.doc: The original's ciphertext content address (lowercase hex).

members.name: plaintextSize
members.doc: The original's plaintext length in bytes.

members.name: action
members.doc: The head manifest's lifecycle action (`create`, `metadata-update`, `delete`, …).

members.name: timestamp
members.doc: RFC3339 authoring timestamp of the head manifest.

members.name: createdByDevice
members.doc: The device that authored it (UUID string), resolved in the signed device directory.

members.name: provenanceHead
members.doc:
The 32-byte provenance head this entry establishes — persist it and pass it back as
[`FfiSyncEntry::local_chain_head`] next time.

members.name: metadata
members.doc:
The decrypted, signature-checked metadata.

`None` exactly when the action mints no metadata blob — a `delete` tombstone or a
`trash-restore`. Those are fully-verified entries that simply carry no metadata, so an
app applies the lifecycle change and leaves the row's metadata as it stands.

declarations.name: FfiAssetMetadata
declarations.doc: The decrypted sidecar's facts, flattened for a catalog upsert.

members.name: sidecarSchema
members.doc: Sidecar schema version.

members.name: contentType
members.doc: The original's MIME type.

members.name: captureTimestamp
members.doc:
RFC3339 capture time the asset is dated by: the user's correction when one is recorded,
else the as-imported value.

members.name: width
members.doc: Pixel width, when the sidecar records dimensions.

members.name: height
members.doc: Pixel height, when the sidecar records dimensions.

members.name: lqipChromahash
members.doc: LQIP chromahash bytes — renderable the instant metadata syncs, at zero extra request.

members.name: lqipDominantColor
members.doc: LQIP dominant colour, as three RGB bytes.

members.name: caption
members.doc: The caption LWW register's current value, if any.

members.name: tags
members.doc: The user-tag OR-set's current members, sorted.

[`FfiError::InvalidArgument`].

owns together with the budget that bounds it. An entry here for `recovery_check_due` is
honoured as a fallback (the later of the two wins) but is not the canonical channel.

declarations.name: evaluateAlerts
declarations.signature: public func evaluateAlerts(input: FfiNotifyInput, now: String) throws -> [FfiAlert]
declarations.doc:
Every alert that is true at `now`, in delivery order.

Pure and offline: no network call, no library open, no clock read — `now` is the caller's, so
the same input always gives the same answer and an app can drive it from a test clock.

# Errors

[`FfiError::InvalidArgument`] if `now` or any instant in `input` is not RFC 3339, or if
`suppressed_until` names something that is not an alert class.

declarations.name: nextAlertDeadline
declarations.signature: public func nextAlertDeadline(input: FfiNotifyInput, now: String) throws -> String?
declarations.doc:
The earliest instant in [`pre_arm_deadlines`] (RFC 3339), or `None` when there is nothing to
arm.

For a host that can hold only one timer. **An app that schedules per class wants
[`pre_arm_deadlines`]**: the minimum discards the later class's alarm, and on a device the app
never runs on again that alert is simply lost.

# Errors

As [`evaluate_alerts`].

declarations.name: preArmDeadlines
declarations.signature: public func preArmDeadlines(input: FfiNotifyInput, now: String) throws -> [FfiClassDeadline]
declarations.doc:
The instant to arm a local notification for, **per class** — the call an app schedules its
`UNCalendarNotificationTrigger` / `AlarmManager` alarms from.

Reconcile your timers against the result: a class present here should hold exactly one alarm
at the returned instant, and a class absent from it should hold none. Recompute after **any**
state change; that is the whole of the arm / re-arm / cancel rule on the client side.

Only the two classes whose deadline a device can compute alone ever appear. The other three
depend on server state and surface at next app launch — a real gap the design accepts.

# Errors

As [`evaluate_alerts`].

declarations.name: p256HardwareDekRoundTrip
declarations.signature: public func p256HardwareDekRoundTrip(hardware: FfiHardwareKeyAgreement, keyAlias: String, mlSeed: Data) throws -> Bool
declarations.doc:
Smoke the **hardware-bound P-256 device encryption key** across the FFI seam:
enroll a key-agreement key in `hardware` under `key_alias`, publish the hybrid public key,
encapsulate a fresh shared secret to it **in software** (the sender side), then
**decapsulate through the element's ECDH**. Returns `true` iff the two secrets match —
proving the element's ECDH composes into the hybrid KEM without the private scalar leaving
hardware. `ml_seed` (32 bytes) is the software-sealed ML-KEM-768 half.

The DEK is not yet wired into workspace creation, so this focused round-trip is the
composition's on-device check — the DEK analogue of
[`FfiWorkspace::create_with_p256_hardware_signer`]. Every step is one `capsule-core` call.

members.signature: suspend fun verifySecondFactor(mfaToken: kotlin.String, totpCode: kotlin.String): FfiSession
members.doc:
Complete a sign-in with the code an authenticator app is showing.

`mfa_token` is what [`FfiLoginOutcome::SecondFactorRequired`] carried. It is good once
and for five minutes.

declarations.name: FfiHardwareKeyAgreement
declarations.doc:
The per-platform **key-agreement** element (Secure Enclave `P256.KeyAgreement`, StrongBox
ECDH, TPM 2.0 ECDH), implemented by native Swift/Kotlin over the uniffi foreign-trait
boundary — the ECDH analogue of [`FfiHardwareSigner`], and this namespace's declaration of
`capsule-core`'s `HardwareKeyAgreement` contract.

It backs the hardware-bound classical half of the device **encryption** key:
the element holds a static P-256 private key and performs the ECDH, so the scalar never
leaves hardware, while Rust drives the software-sealed ML-KEM-768 half and the hybrid
combiner. Failures reuse [`FfiHardwareSignerError`], exactly as core's trait reuses its
signer error.

members.name: enroll
members.doc:
Generate (or bind to) the hardware P-256 key-agreement keypair for `key_alias`,
returning its public key as **uncompressed SEC1** (`0x04‖x‖y`, 65 bytes). Idempotent per
alias.

members.name: publicKey
members.doc: The uncompressed-SEC1 P-256 public key for an already-enrolled `key_alias`.

members.name: keyAgreement
members.signature: fun keyAgreement(keyAlias: kotlin.String, peerPublic: kotlin.ByteArray): kotlin.ByteArray
members.doc:
ECDH against `peer_public` (the sender's ephemeral P-256 public key, uncompressed SEC1)
with the hardware key for `key_alias`, returning the **raw 32-byte shared secret** (the
big-endian x-coordinate, before any KDF).

members.name: assertNonExportable
members.doc:
Non-exportability assertion: a conforming element MUST refuse to reveal the private
bytes, returning [`FfiHardwareSignerError::Exportable`] if they can be read.

declarations.name: FfiHardwareSigner
declarations.doc:
The per-platform secure element (Secure Enclave, StrongBox, TPM), implemented by native
Swift/Kotlin over the uniffi foreign-trait boundary.

The byte shapes are fixed by the constructor the element is handed to, not by the trait:

- [`FfiWorkspace::create_with_p256_hardware_signer`] — the **P-256** shape shipping
elements actually provide: [`enroll`](Self::enroll) /
[`classical_public_key`](Self::classical_public_key) return a SEC1 public key and
[`sign_classical`](Self::sign_classical) a **DER-encoded ECDSA** signature over
`SHA-256(msg)`.
- [`FfiWorkspace::create_with_hardware_signer`] — the **Ed25519** shape: a 32-byte public
key and a 64-byte signature over `msg`. No shipping secure element holds Ed25519 keys, so
this is the software/TPM reference path.

Either way Rust composes the classical half with a software-sealed ML-DSA-65 half into the
published hybrid device key.

members.name: enroll
members.doc:
Generate (or bind to) the hardware keypair for `key_alias`, returning its public key in
the constructor's shape: a SEC1 P-256 key for
[`FfiWorkspace::create_with_p256_hardware_signer`], a 32-byte Ed25519 key for
[`FfiWorkspace::create_with_hardware_signer`]. Idempotent per alias.

members.name: classicalPublicKey
members.doc:
The public key for an already-enrolled `key_alias`, in the same constructor-dependent
shape [`enroll`](Self::enroll) returns (SEC1 P-256, or 32-byte Ed25519).

members.name: signClassical
members.signature: fun signClassical(keyAlias: kotlin.String, msg: kotlin.ByteArray): kotlin.ByteArray
members.doc:
Sign `msg` with the hardware key for `key_alias`, in the constructor's shape: a
DER-encoded ECDSA signature over `SHA-256(msg)` for
[`FfiWorkspace::create_with_p256_hardware_signer`], a 64-byte Ed25519 signature over
`msg` for [`FfiWorkspace::create_with_hardware_signer`].

members.name: assertNonExportable
members.doc:
Non-exportability assertion: a conforming element MUST refuse to reveal the private
bytes, returning [`FfiHardwareSignerError::Exportable`] if they can be read.

declarations.name: FfiSession
declarations.signature: open class FfiSession: Disposable, AutoCloseable, FfiSessionInterface
declarations.doc:
An authenticated session handle. Owns the SDK token store internally (auto
pre-flight refresh, single-flight, `401`-retry-once); **no token ever crosses
the FFI boundary**. Every flow rides this handle.

members.name: escrowGet
members.doc:
Fetch this account's escrow blob (`GET /v1/auth/escrow`) as opaque canonical CBOR — the
bytes [`FfiWorkspace::verify_escrow_blob`](FfiWorkspace::verify_escrow_blob) checks and
a recovery flow unwraps.

No escrow enrolled yet is [`FfiError::Escrow`] carrying `error.escrow.not_stored` — the
code that separates "set up a recovery key" from "we could not read the one you have".
A refused credential is [`FfiError::Auth`].

members.name: escrowPut
members.signature: suspend fun escrowPut(apiBaseUrl: kotlin.String, blob: kotlin.ByteArray): FfiEscrowStored
members.doc:
Store or replace this account's **master-key escrow blob** (`PUT /v1/auth/escrow`).
`blob` is the opaque canonical CBOR
[`FfiWorkspace::escrow_blob`](FfiWorkspace::escrow_blob) minted — the master key itself
never crosses this boundary in either direction.

Single active escrow: the server replaces any prior blob in the same transaction, so the
secret a rotation retired unwraps nothing.

`api_base_url` is the API root the session authenticates against (the per-call endpoint
convention this surface already uses for `sync_pull`). A URL operation paths cannot hang
off is [`FfiError::InvalidArgument`]; a refused credential is [`FfiError::Auth`], so a
caller re-authenticates rather than retrying; everything else is
[`FfiError::Escrow`] with the server's `error.escrow.*` code when it sent one.

The answer says what the store did: [`FfiEscrowStored::replaced`] separates "recovery
set up" from "recovery key replaced" (the previous secret has stopped working).

members.name: fetchBlobToPath
members.signature: suspend fun fetchBlobToPath(blobBaseUrl: kotlin.String, hash: kotlin.String, size: kotlin.ULong, path: kotlin.String)
members.doc:
**Fetch** the blob at content address `hash` (`size` bytes, as the sync feed's
[`FfiBlobRef`] declares) into the file at `path`, created or truncated.

The blob streams to disk in bounded `Range` windows, so memory is bounded by one window
whatever the blob's size, and its content address is checked as it lands. On any error
the file is removed: a path this returns `Ok` for holds exactly the verified ciphertext.
A session that cannot authorize the fetch is [`FfiError::Auth`], so the app signs in
again; every other failure is [`FfiError::Fetch`].

`blob_base_url` is the root the blob route hangs off (`{blob_base_url}/blob/{hash}`),
the server's `/v1` root.

members.name: fetchDeviceDirectory
members.signature: suspend fun fetchDeviceDirectory(apiBaseUrl: kotlin.String, userId: kotlin.String, pinnedUserIk: kotlin.ByteArray): kotlin.ByteArray
members.doc:
Fetch a user's signed device directory, **verified under `pinned_user_ik`** (the bytes
[`FfiWorkspace::user_ik_public`](FfiWorkspace::user_ik_public) returns) before it is
handed back. A document that does not verify is an error, never a return value.

members.name: isAuthenticated
members.doc: Whether the session currently holds tokens (`false` after logout).

members.name: logout
members.doc: Revoke the session server-side and clear the local store (idempotent).

members.name: publishDeviceDirectory
members.signature: suspend fun publishDeviceDirectory(apiBaseUrl: kotlin.String, directoryCbor: kotlin.ByteArray, userIk: kotlin.ByteArray): kotlin.ULong
members.doc:
Publish this device's **signed device directory**, returning the `directory_version` the
server now stores. `directory_cbor` is the opaque document
[`FfiWorkspace::signed_device_directory`](FfiWorkspace::signed_device_directory)
produced; it travels verbatim, because re-encoding it would detach it from the signature
it carries. `user_ik` is the account's user identity **public** key the document is
signed under — the bytes [`FfiWorkspace::user_ik_public`](FfiWorkspace::user_ik_public)
returns — which the server anchors on first publish and verifies every publish against.

Publish when the document changes (a device enrolled or revoked). The version must
advance — republishing an unchanged document answers the version-conflict code.

members.name: pushAsset
members.signature: suspend fun pushAsset(workspace: FfiWorkspace, assetId: kotlin.String): FfiPushReport
members.doc:
**Push** one sealed asset of `workspace` — every blob of its bundle, in ladder order
(provenance and metadata, then derivative manifests and derivatives, then the
original) — driving `capsule_sdk::push::push_bundle` inside the SDK.

The original never crosses the boundary: its ciphertext is re-derived from the
plaintext on disk one upload chunk window at a time, so memory is bounded by the
transfer window whatever the original's size. The workspace lock is held only while the
bundle is built, never across the network.

Every blob is driven; one the server already holds answers `duplicate_blob` and comes
back [`FfiUploadOutcome::AlreadyStored`], so pushing twice is safe. The album must
already be provisioned on the server.

**A create the server refused is re-sealed and retried once** (issue #822). When the
album's epoch moved past the one the asset was sealed under, the server refuses its
create for good; if this device holds a newer epoch, the asset is re-sealed at it
(`Workspace::reseal_create`) and pushed again, once. A second refusal fails the push.
When this device holds no newer epoch the push fails with [`FfiError::Upload`] carrying
the server's code and a detail saying there is no newer epoch to re-seal at, and the
asset stays local. That detail names no missing key: the refusal may have had nothing to
do with the epoch (a revoked device, withdrawn write access), or another device rotated
the album and its key has not reached this one yet.

members.name: syncPull
members.signature: suspend fun syncPull(apiBaseUrl: kotlin.String, cursor: kotlin.ByteArray, pageSize: kotlin.UInt): FfiSyncPage
members.doc:
Pull one page of the key-free sync feed after `cursor` from `api_base_url`
(`http[s]://host:port`). Pass an empty `cursor` for the first page; persist and pass
back `next_cursor` to advance. The bearer rides the `Authorization` header
(auto-refreshed); it never crosses the FFI boundary.

The parameter is the **API base URL** now, not a gRPC endpoint: the feed is
`GET /v1/sync` on the same origin as every other call.

members.name: upload
members.signature: suspend fun upload(request: FfiUploadRequest, data: kotlin.ByteArray): FfiUploadOutcome
members.doc:
Upload a full ciphertext blob (`data`) under `request`, driving the adaptive,
resumable protocol with the code-driven recovery matrix.

`data` crosses the boundary whole, so this is for blobs an app already holds in memory.
To push a sealed asset, original included, use [`push_asset`](Self::push_asset), which
never holds the original whole.

members.name: uploadStatus
members.doc:
Query an upload session's progress (`HEAD /upload/{id}`). `None` means the
session is gone (discarded/expired/never-existent).

declarations.name: FfiWorkspace
declarations.signature: open class FfiWorkspace: Disposable, AutoCloseable, FfiWorkspaceInterface
declarations.doc:
A Capsule workspace, callable from Swift/Kotlin: the durable library at a filesystem root
plus everything an app does with it.

`Workspace` mutates through `&mut self` while uniffi objects expose only `&self`; the
`Mutex` supplies the interior mutability and serializes concurrent foreign calls.

members.name: create
members.signature: @Throws(FfiException::class) fun create(root: kotlin.String, passphrase: kotlin.ByteArray, tier: FfiDeviceTier, client: FfiClientBuild): FfiWorkspace
members.doc:
**Enroll**: create a brand-new library at `root`, guarded by `passphrase` at the
Argon2id cost for `tier`. Mints the account, the device key, and the signed device
directory, and seeds the durable album keystore.

`client` is the app's own build identity: every manifest this workspace authors then
reports `client_id/semver+commit` rather than the bare `capsule-core` default.

members.name: createWithHardwareSigner
members.signature: @Throws(FfiException::class) fun createWithHardwareSigner(root: kotlin.String, passphrase: kotlin.ByteArray, tier: FfiDeviceTier, hardware: FfiHardwareSigner, keyAlias: kotlin.String, mlSeed: kotlin.ByteArray, client: FfiClientBuild): FfiWorkspace
members.doc:
**Enroll with a hardware-bound Ed25519 device key**: as [`create`](Self::create), but
the classical half of the device signing key is produced by `hardware` under
`key_alias` over **Ed25519** (a 32-byte public key, 64-byte signatures). The
post-quantum ML-DSA-65 half is the software-sealed `ml_seed` (32 bytes).

No shipping secure element holds Ed25519 keys, so this is the software/TPM reference
composition; phones use
[`create_with_p256_hardware_signer`](Self::create_with_p256_hardware_signer). It is the
same core call (`HardwareBackedSigner::enroll`) reached through this namespace's
[`FfiHardwareSigner`] seam.

members.name: createWithP256HardwareSigner
members.signature: @Throws(FfiException::class) fun createWithP256HardwareSigner(root: kotlin.String, passphrase: kotlin.ByteArray, tier: FfiDeviceTier, hardware: FfiHardwareSigner, keyAlias: kotlin.String, mlSeed: kotlin.ByteArray, client: FfiClientBuild): FfiWorkspace
members.doc:
**Enroll with a hardware-bound device key**: as [`create`](Self::create), but the
classical half of the device signing key is produced by `hardware` (a native Secure
Enclave / StrongBox / TPM element) under `key_alias`, over **ECDSA-P256** — the
composition shipping secure elements actually provide, none of which do Ed25519. The
post-quantum ML-DSA-65 half is the software-sealed `ml_seed` (32 bytes).

The published device key carries the P-256 tag and `verify_asset` dispatches on it, so
this is constructor parity with `capsule-core`'s own
`create_with_p256_hardware_signer` — the same core call, reached through this
namespace's [`FfiHardwareSigner`] seam.

members.name: open
members.signature: @Throws(FfiException::class) fun open(root: kotlin.String, passphrase: kotlin.ByteArray, tier: FfiDeviceTier, client: FfiClientBuild): FfiWorkspace
members.doc:
**Open** the existing library at `root` under `passphrase`, restoring its album keys and
authorities, every managed asset, and the `add_id` counter from disk. This is
what makes an app relaunch resume rather than re-enroll.

members.name: albums
members.doc: Every album this workspace holds key material for.

members.name: applySyncEntry
members.doc:
**Sync-apply**: verify one remote feed entry through the `verify_asset` chokepoint,
bind and decrypt its metadata blob, and return either the facts to upsert or a named
quarantine/hold verdict.

Never silently drops and never silently accepts: a refused entry is a
[`FfiSyncApplyOutcome::Quarantined`] the app must surface, not an error that aborts the
page. Errors are reserved for a failure of this workspace itself.

members.name: applySyncEntryFromFile
members.signature: fun applySyncEntryFromFile(entry: FfiSyncHead, ciphertextPath: kotlin.String): FfiSyncApplyOutcome
members.doc:
[`apply_sync_entry`](Self::apply_sync_entry) for an entry whose original ciphertext is
the file at `ciphertext_path` — the one
[`FfiSession::fetch_blob_to_path`](crate::ffi::FfiSession::fetch_blob_to_path) wrote —
read in memory bounded by one STREAM chunk whatever the original's size.

The same chokepoint and verdicts: the file is hashed, and that digest is what the
content-integrity step checks against the manifest's content address, so a file that is
not the committed ciphertext is quarantined as `Rejected.CiphertextHashMismatch`, as
`apply_sync_entry` quarantines those bytes. Nothing is written anywhere.

A malformed `album_id` or `local_chain_head` is refused before the file is opened, so a
bad argument never costs a read of the original. The file is hashed before the workspace
is locked, so other verbs are not held up while a large original is read.

members.name: assetIds
members.doc: Every managed asset id (UUID strings).

members.name: createAlbum
members.doc:
Create an album (minting AMK_v1, its write-tier and admin keys, and an attested
authority, then persisting the keystore). Returns the album id.

members.name: defaultAlbumId
members.doc:
The default album's id, derived deterministically from the account master key — so every
device of this account computes the same value with nothing to synchronize.

members.name: deviceId
members.doc:
This device's id (UUID string) — the `created_by_device` of every manifest it authors,
and the id to report as the session's `device_id`.

members.name: ensureAlbum
members.signature: fun ensureAlbum(albumId: kotlin.String, name: kotlin.String): kotlin.String
members.doc:
Resolve `album_id` to the album this workspace already holds, or create it under `name`.
This is the verb first-run wiring wants for the default album: it is idempotent across
relaunches, where [`create_album`](Self::create_album) would refuse.

members.name: escrowBlob
members.signature: fun escrowBlob(recoverySecret: kotlin.ByteArray, tier: FfiDeviceTier): kotlin.ByteArray
members.doc:
Mint the **master-key escrow blob** under `recovery_secret`, as opaque canonical CBOR —
the bytes [`FfiSession::escrow_put`](crate::ffi::FfiSession::escrow_put) stores.

The master key never crosses this boundary: it is wrapped inside `capsule-core` and only
the wrapped blob comes out. `recovery_secret` is the ≥128-bit secret shown to the user
exactly once at first-device enrollment.

members.name: openSyncedOriginal
members.signature: fun openSyncedOriginal(entry: FfiSyncHead, ciphertextPath: kotlin.String, destinationPath: kotlin.String): FfiOpenedOriginal
members.doc:
**Open a synced original** from the ciphertext file at `ciphertext_path` to its plaintext
at `destination_path`, in memory bounded by a few STREAM chunks whatever its size.

The entry goes through the chokepoint as
[`apply_sync_entry_from_file`](Self::apply_sync_entry_from_file) would take it, then the
file is hashed while it is decrypted: it opens only if it is the ciphertext the manifest
commits to, every chunk authenticates, and the plaintext hashes to the signed sidecar's
digest. The plaintext is written to a hidden staging file beside the destination and
renamed into place only once all of that holds, so `destination_path` is untouched by
any other verdict and never holds a partial or unverified original. An existing file there
is replaced only by a verified one.

The workspace stays locked while the original decrypts.

# Errors

[`FfiError::Workspace`] when a file cannot be read or written, or the workspace itself
fails; [`FfiError::InvalidArgument`] for a malformed entry or a destination with no file
name. A refused entry is a verdict, never an error.

members.name: provenanceHead
members.doc:
The asset's **head provenance record** as opaque canonical CBOR — the exact bytes the
`provenance` blob carries, the feed serves back as `manifest_cbor`, and a receiving
device runs through [`apply_sync_entry`](Self::apply_sync_entry).

The record wraps the head signed manifest with its chain position. That wrapper is not
optional: the server's chain head is the SHA-256 of these bytes while a client's next
`prior_provenance_hash` is the record's own hash, so the bare manifest is the one
encoding under which no lifecycle op can ever chain. Canonical CBOR is deterministic, so
the manifest inside is byte-identical to its own signed bytes — nothing is re-authored
and the two signatures still verify over exactly what they covered.

Use [`signed_manifest`](Self::signed_manifest) when the *manifest* is what is wanted.

members.name: readPlaintext
members.doc:
The plaintext bytes of a managed asset (what a gallery renders for a locally-held
original).

members.name: sealAsset
members.signature: fun sealAsset(albumId: kotlin.String, fileName: kotlin.String, bytes: kotlin.ByteArray): kotlin.String
members.doc:
**Seal + import**: take bytes the app already holds (a PhotoKit / MediaStore export),
derive the file key, STREAM-encrypt, author and sign the create manifest, seal the
signed sidecar into its metadata blob, append the provenance chain, and self-verify
through the `verify_asset` chokepoint. Returns the asset id.

`file_name` is consulted for its extension and nothing else. One call, one core call:
the whole sealing order is `capsule-core`'s.

members.name: signedDeviceDirectory
members.doc:
This workspace's **signed device directory** as opaque canonical CBOR — the bytes
[`FfiSession::publish_device_directory`](crate::ffi::FfiSession::publish_device_directory)
sends. Until this is published, every asset this device signs is an unknown device to
every other device, so first-device enrollment publishes before it uploads.

members.name: signedManifest
members.doc:
The asset's **head signed manifest** as opaque canonical CBOR.

This is a serialization of an already-signed structure, not a re-authoring: the two
signatures the manifest carries are covered by these bytes, which is why they travel
verbatim and are never re-modeled on any wire.

**Not what the sync feed carries** — that is
[`provenance_head`](Self::provenance_head), the record that wraps this manifest with its
chain position. Handing these bytes to
[`apply_sync_entry`](Self::apply_sync_entry) is refused as malformed.

members.name: uploadBlobs
members.doc:
Everything needed to push one sealed asset, in ladder order: for each blob, the
`POST /upload` body (manifest envelope projected per the server's invariant-15 rule)
and the bytes. Feed each straight to
[`FfiSession::upload`](crate::ffi::FfiSession::upload).

The index tier (`T0`) is **two** blobs — the provenance record then the sealed metadata
blob — because the server publishes an asset to other devices only once it holds both
roles. Push all of them: an app that stopped after the metadata blob would upload an
asset no device, its own included, could ever see.

The original's ciphertext is re-derived from the manifest's recorded nonce prefix and
gated on the manifest's own content address, so what reaches the network is what the
signed manifest vouches for.

Every blob comes back whole, the original included. To push without holding the
original in memory, use [`FfiSession::push_asset`](crate::ffi::FfiSession::push_asset).

members.name: userId
members.doc: The account owner's user id (UUID string).

members.name: userIkPublic
members.doc:
This account's user identity **public** key — the pin a fetched device directory is
verified against.

members.name: verifyAsset
members.doc:
Run the `verify_asset` chokepoint over a managed asset, regenerating its ciphertext
deterministically. This is the same single chokepoint sync-apply routes through — it is
exposed here so an app can re-check its own library (an integrity sweep), never as a
second verification path.

members.name: verifyEscrowBlob
members.signature: fun verifyEscrowBlob(blob: kotlin.ByteArray, recoverySecret: kotlin.ByteArray): kotlin.Boolean
members.doc:
Local, network-free check that `recovery_secret` still opens `blob` to *this* device's
master key — the recovery verification cadence's predicate. `blob` is the canonical CBOR
[`FfiSession::escrow_get`](crate::ffi::FfiSession::escrow_get) returns.

A `false` is not necessarily a wrong secret: the cached blob may be stale after a
rotation on another device, so refresh it and re-check once before telling the user
anything.

declarations.doc: One album this workspace holds key material for.

members.doc:

members.doc:

scheduler with
[`RecoveryCadence::notify_facts`](crate::recovery::RecoveryCadence::notify_facts) rather
than computing it here. `None` before recovery is set up, which ignores the other three
`recovery_*` fields.

members.doc:
When an active snooze on the recovery prompt expires (RFC 3339), if one is active. A
snooze ending *before* `recovery_next_due` does not make the check due earlier. This is
the canonical place to snooze the recovery check — not
[`suppressed_until`](Self::suppressed_until), which is for the other five classes.

non-blocking badge: still reported, no longer pre-armed.

declaring the secret lost). Surfaces as the alert's `recovery` parameter, so the app
routes into the re-wrap flow instead of rendering a routine verification prompt.

members.doc: How many guest drops are awaiting review and adoption.

members.name: suppressedUntil
members.doc:
Per-class **snooze**: class wire name (`sync_stale`, …) to the RFC 3339 instant the
snooze runs until, exclusive. A class snoozed past `now` reports nothing, and its alarm
is **deferred to the snooze end** rather than cancelled — a class snoozed after it fired
must fire again when the snooze expires. Use [`disabled`](Self::disabled) to turn a class
off; do not encode that as a far-future instant here. An unrecognized class name is an
[`FfiError::InvalidArgument`].

**This map is for the other five classes.** Recovery snoozing belongs in
[`recovery_snoozed_until`](Self::recovery_snoozed_until), which the cadence scheduler
owns together with the budget that bounds it. An entry here for `recovery_check_due` is
honoured as a fallback (the later of the two wins) but is not the canonical channel.

members.name: disabled
members.doc:
Per-class **disable**: the wire names of the classes the user turned off. They report
nothing and hold no alarm, at any instant. Disabling suppresses the warning and never
the behavior. An unrecognized class name is an [`FfiError::InvalidArgument`].

declarations.doc:
One transferable blob of a sealed asset, paired with the `POST /upload` body that declares
it. Hand [`request`](Self::request) and [`bytes`](Self::bytes) straight to

declarations.name: evaluateAlerts
declarations.signature: @Throws(FfiException::class) fun evaluateAlerts(input: FfiNotifyInput, now: kotlin.String): List<FfiAlert>
declarations.doc:
Every alert that is true at `now`, in delivery order.

Pure and offline: no network call, no library open, no clock read — `now` is the caller's, so
the same input always gives the same answer and an app can drive it from a test clock.

# Errors

[`FfiError::InvalidArgument`] if `now` or any instant in `input` is not RFC 3339, or if
`suppressed_until` names something that is not an alert class.

declarations.name: nextAlertDeadline
declarations.signature: @Throws(FfiException::class) fun nextAlertDeadline(input: FfiNotifyInput, now: kotlin.String): kotlin.String?
declarations.doc:
The earliest instant in [`pre_arm_deadlines`] (RFC 3339), or `None` when there is nothing to
arm.

For a host that can hold only one timer. **An app that schedules per class wants
[`pre_arm_deadlines`]**: the minimum discards the later class's alarm, and on a device the app
never runs on again that alert is simply lost.

# Errors

As [`evaluate_alerts`].

declarations.name: preArmDeadlines
declarations.signature: @Throws(FfiException::class) fun preArmDeadlines(input: FfiNotifyInput, now: kotlin.String): List<FfiClassDeadline>
declarations.doc:
The instant to arm a local notification for, **per class** — the call an app schedules its
`UNCalendarNotificationTrigger` / `AlarmManager` alarms from.

Reconcile your timers against the result: a class present here should hold exactly one alarm
at the returned instant, and a class absent from it should hold none. Recompute after **any**
state change; that is the whole of the arm / re-arm / cancel rule on the client side.

Only the two classes whose deadline a device can compute alone ever appear. The other three
depend on server state and surface at next app launch — a real gap the design accepts.

# Errors

As [`evaluate_alerts`].

declarations.name: p256HardwareDekRoundTrip
declarations.signature: @Throws(FfiException::class) fun p256HardwareDekRoundTrip(hardware: FfiHardwareKeyAgreement, keyAlias: kotlin.String, mlSeed: kotlin.ByteArray): kotlin.Boolean
declarations.doc:
Smoke the **hardware-bound P-256 device encryption key** across the FFI seam:
enroll a key-agreement key in `hardware` under `key_alias`, publish the hybrid public key,
encapsulate a fresh shared secret to it **in software** (the sender side), then
**decapsulate through the element's ECDH**. Returns `true` iff the two secrets match —
proving the element's ECDH composes into the hybrid KEM without the private scalar leaving
hardware. `ml_seed` (32 bytes) is the software-sealed ML-KEM-768 half.

The DEK is not yet wired into workspace creation, so this focused round-trip is the
composition's on-device check — the DEK analogue of
[`FfiWorkspace::create_with_p256_hardware_signer`]. Every step is one `capsule-core` call.
